entry.title: Understanding Gradients: The Engine Behind Neural Network Learning
entry.summary: In the previous article, we explored activation functions and visualized them using Python. Now, let’s see what gradients are. Neural networks use activation functions to transform inputs inside them. But if a neural network gives a wrong output, how does it know what to fix? This is where gradients come in. Imagine you are walking on a hill. If the ground is steep, you can feel which direction goes up or down. If the ground is almost flat, it is hard to tell where to go. A gradient can be simply thought of as a number that tells us how steep a curve is at a point. How does this apply in the case of neural networks? Let’s see.
